subject: Request: short-term high-priority lane for Black Friday pilot
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@fastcart.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-09T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: short-term high-priority lane for Black Friday pilot

Hi Naomi / Ben —

We’re ramping up a limited Black Friday pilot (FastCart Checkout Assist) and expect a very narrow, high-intensity traffic window on 2025-11-28 through 2025-12-02 (peak forecasts attached). We’d like to request a short-term, guaranteed priority throughput lane (isolated token pool or equivalent) to ensure latency stays under 120ms p50 during the pilot while we validate UX.

Key asks:
- Dedicated priority pool able to sustain ~3.5M tokens/day during peak days (est. 15x baseline).
- Temporary exception to fairness-based throttling for 11/27 00:00 UTC through 12/03 23:59 UTC.
- Fallback routing to a lower-cost model once pilot window completes.

We can work with an agreed temporary surcharge; procurement timeline is tight — we need confirmation by 2025-12-11 to finalize our vendor signoff.

Attachment: capacity_plan.xlsx (estimated traffic curves + business impact)

Thanks —
Elena Morales
Head of Product Integrations, FastCart
elena@fastcart.com

Naomi / team / Elena —

We can support this as a short-term operational carveout but there are three considerations:

1) Capacity surface: we propose provisioning a dedicated priority token pool sized to sustain 4M tokens/day (buffered for safety) for the 2025-11-27 -> 2025-12-03 window. That will be implemented as a scoped queue with higher scheduling priority and eviction-protected KV caches.

2) Fairness policy adjustment: we can suspend fairness tiebreaks for requests originating from FastCart routes during the window, but we require an explicit SLA addendum noting the temporary nature and the potential momentary impact on best-effort customers in the same region.

3) Billing/Surcharge: ops will apply a temporary usage surcharge; Marissa, can you run a quick delta to surface the estimated incremental invoice?

I attached a short ops plan for how we'll stand up the pool and the rollback steps. This requires a manual playbook run and a one-time ops on-call for 48 hours around the peak start.

Attachment: proposed-ops-plan.pdf

If that sounds OK to Elena, we can prepare a short DocuSign amendment and a HubSpot deal update.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Elena Morales <elena@fastcart.com>
Date: 2025-12-09T13:41:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Request: short-term high-priority lane for Black Friday pilot

Quick technical notes:

- Model variants: to preserve latency we’ll route priority-lane requests to the same model family but a quantized variant (Q4/Q5) during the window; this keeps p50 under target while controlling GPU memory. We’ll keep the production (non-priority) routing intact as fallback.
- KV cache: we’ll seed persistent prefix caches for the pilot flows to avoid cold-start penalties.
- Monitoring: must add synthetic probes that kick at T-minus 48h and T-minus 2h; set automated rollback at sustained p95 > 800ms for more than 3 minutes.
